title: Stabilize embedding metric behavior across SDK versions and server-side adapters
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem summary:
Customers rely on both cosine and dot-product semantics for embedding similarity across SDK versions and community clients. Recent changes to internal normalization (automatic L2 normalization for some model families) and a server-side metric adapter introduced subtle behavioral differences: identical vector pairs sometimes changed score by >1e-3, and downstream reranking precision at top-5 changed for a small portion of queries.

Scope and goals:
1) Define and enforce a stable, explicit contract for how Redwood computes embedding similarity (cosine vs dot) at the API surface across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.
2) Implement a compatibility layer so older SDKs/clients that assumed pre-change behavior continue to get deterministic scores unless they opt in to new semantics.
3) Repair and harden server-side normalization logic so it is numerically stable, perf-conscious, and documented.
4) Add telemetry, tests, and a gradual rollout plan to measure impact on quality and latency.

Why this matters now:
- Reranking customers are sensitive to small score shifts (precision@k regressions can break UIs).
- Private deployments need a deterministic rule they can pin to for audits.
- Inconsistent semantics across SDKs creates support overhead and migration churn.

Non-goals:
- Changing default model embeddings or retraining models.
- Rewriting customer reranker logic; we will offer migration guidance instead.
acceptance_criteria: Define public API contract describing difference between 'metric=cosine' and 'metric=dot' and the treatment of input norms
Server returns identical scores (within 1e-8 relative) for a defined compatibility mode compared to pre-change baseline for a representative test corpus
New normalization path reduces per-request CPU overhead by <=5% at p95 for embedding-only endpoints compared to prior implementation, or document trade-offs if slightly slower
Telemetry shows no statistically significant regression in precision@5 and precision@10 on the production reranker testset after gradual rollout (95% CI), or we can successfully rollback
Public SDK changelog and migration guide published and linked from API docs
tasks: Audit current code paths that perform normalization: runtime embedding pipeline, Local adapter, and compatibility shim
Design deterministic compatibility mode API flag: e.g., 'metric=cosine&norm_mode=preserve' and spec for parameter precedence
Implement server-side normalization utility with stable algorithms (Kahan-like reduction where needed) and explicit epsilon handling for zero norms
Add end-to-end unit tests and numeric regression tests against archived baseline vectors (small corpus from reranker suite)
Add telemetry: record metric used, input norms distribution, pre/post-normalization checksum, and per-request score delta buckets
Create SDK patches for JS and Python exposing metric and norm_mode flags and adding integration tests
Run canary rollout on 5% of traffic with automatic rollback thresholds for precision@5 and latency
Prepare and publish migration guide and release notes; coordinate with Support and Solutions teams
comments: 2026-02-20 Maya Chen: Created ticket after a customer reported flapping in top-k reranker results following SDK upgrade. Attached initial repro vectors and links to support ticket.

2026-02-24 Arjun Patel: Early audit shows two places performing implicit normalization: 1) embedding runtime pipeline (normalize_for_model) and 2) re-ranking adapter that assumed embeddings were already unit-norm. These double-normalize in some flows. Drafting safe single-source-of-truth for normalization.

2026-02-28 Design decision: Use explicit API parameter precedence: query params override saved request metadata; default behavior remains 'compatibility' for requests without explicit metric to avoid surprising customers. Documented in API spec PR.

2026-03-03 Eng note: Implemented stable_l2_norm function using compensated summation and thresholding for near-zero norms. Unit tests added verifying numerical stability on 1e-12 magnitude vectors. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4891

2026-03-05 Performance test: microbenchmarks show stable_l2_norm is ~2.7% slower in pure Python path but <1% in C++ runtime due to vectorized kernels. We will ship optimized kernel fallback for hot paths.
2026-03-07 QA: Regression test against archived reranker baseline (10k vector pairs) shows mean score delta reduced from 3.2e-4 to 8.7e-9 in compatibility mode. Precision@5 unchanged within noise.
2026-03-09 PM note: Coordinated with SDK leads. JS SDK will default to 'metric=unspecified' preserving legacy; new explicit flags will be in 1.6.0 release. Support article drafted.

2026-03-10 Rollout plan: canary 5% start 2026-03-15; monitor precision@5, score-delta histogram, avg token latency for rerank endpoint, and SLO errors. Auto-rollback if precision@5 drops by >=1.5% or p95 latency increases by >=20%
